title: Tone-buffer inspector
blurb: Exercises eight normative RTCDTMFSender rules on fresh WebRTC loopbacks: pre-negotiation and recvonly canInsertDTMF, InvalidStateError, InvalidCharacterError, uppercase normalization, duration/gap clamping, comma pause, buffer replacement, and null video sender dtmf.
question: Does Chromium's RTCRtpSender.dtmf enforce every WebRTC 1.0 RTCDTMFSender boundary rule including exception types, timing clamps, comma pauses, and mid-stream buffer replacement?
result: Verified in Chrome 153 headless (desktop and mobile): 8/8 normative checks passed. Clamped 10 ms / 5 ms input measured ~103 ms spacing, comma pause measured ~2030 ms, mid-play replacement produced '1|9|""', and video sender dtmf was null.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12 (desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740); not re-run in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Clamped minimum timing (40 ms duration / 30 ms gap) measures ~103 ms between tonechange events in Chromium instead of ~70 ms
friction.repro: Run the duration/interToneGap clamping check with insertDTMF('12', 10, 5); Chromium clamps to 40/30 ms but fires successive tonechange events ~103 ms apart (~duration + 2 * gap).
friction.workaround: Allow timing tolerance above duration + interToneGap when testing or coordinating DTMF bursts with remote IVR timeouts.
